posts.title: Tesla China's August wholesale sales total 86,166, snapping 3-month sequential gain streak
posts.summary:
Tesla China's August wholesale sales rose 3.57% year-on-year but fell 7.92% from July.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Tesla China's August wholesale sales reached 86,166 units, a 3.57% year-on-year increase but a 7.92% decline from July, ending a three-month streak of sequential growth.
Tesla's performance lagged behind the broader Chinese new energy vehicle market, which grew 16% year-on-year and 4% sequentially in August.
Despite the monthly dip, Tesla China's year-to-date wholesale sales total 647,694 units, representing a 25.63% increase compared to the same period in 2025.
Intensifying local competition remains a headwind, with Leapmotor's global deliveries exceeding Tesla China's wholesale figures for the third consecutive month.

posts.title: Nio's Shenji M97 chip may enter Geely's supply chain, report says
posts.summary:
Geely is evaluating the M97 chip, jointly developed by Nio and Axera, for a dual-chip L3 autonomous driving system.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely is evaluating Nio's Shenji M97 chip for a dual-chip L3 autonomous driving system, marking a significant potential expansion for Nio's semiconductor unit.
The M97 chip, developed by Nio's GeniTech and Axera, offers 700 TOPS of computing power and is positioned to compete directly with Horizon Robotics' Journey 6P.
While no formal supply agreement is confirmed, the collaboration represents a strategic shift for Nio to monetize its proprietary chip architecture with third-party automakers.
Shenji has already secured a government nomination for an edge-inference project in Hefei, signaling growing external validation of its technology.

posts.summary:

September 2nd, 2026 - 
								By: Keysight
								
							
						
Edge AI systems increasingly make real-time decisions in cameras, robotics, vehicles, and industrial equipment.
These systems often rely on neural processing units, graphics processors, or other hardware accelerators to perform inference efficiently.
However, continued operation does not necessarily mean that the system’s perception remains trustworthy.
The white paper examines a particularly dangerous failure mode: an edge AI system that remains active and appears healthy while silently accepting an incorrect view of its environment.
